item.title: Statistics, ML & AI events
item.description:
Seminar series and local calendars

Biostatistics, bioinformatics, and health data science

  • Emory Biostatistics and Bioinformatics — The BIOS Beat — the department’s biweekly newsletter lists research events and webinars in biostatistics and bioinformatics. Use the Stay In Touch section for current and past issues.
  • Georgia CTSA Biostatistics, Epidemiology, and Research Design (BERD) Research Forum — a recurring forum connecting statistical methods with clinical and translational research across Emory, Georgia Tech, Morehouse School of Medicine, and UGA. Themes have included clinical trials, wearable data, and AI in health care; check the organizer for the next edition.
  • Emory Biomedical Informatics Seminar Series — research talks on clinical prediction, medical imaging, electronic health records, and AI for patient care. The calendar also links to Georgia CTSA informatics lunch-and-learn events; attendance formats vary by session.
  • Emory Tuberculosis Research Advancement Center events — seminars and workshops connecting infectious-disease research with epidemiology, real-world evidence, and AI/ML. Consult individual announcements for local viewing locations and online participation.

Atlanta and nearby Georgia

  • Georgia State Statistics Seminar — statistics talks organized by Yichuan Zhao. The Mathematics and Statistics calendar provides departmental event announcements.
  • Georgia Tech ISyE Statistics Seminar — statistical theory, methods, and applications.
  • Machine Learning at Georgia Tech — current ML seminar and robotics seminar schedules.
  • Georgia Tech IDEaS seminars and events — AI foundations, machine learning, and high-performance computing talks and workshops.
  • Georgia Tech CSIP Seminar — signal processing, statistical learning, and information theory.
  • Emory Data Science lecture series — data science, causal inference, and applications across research disciplines.
  • Emory CODES seminars — computational and data-enabled science, with an associated student scientific-computing seminar.
  • University of Georgia Statistics events — colloquia, lectures, and statistics events in Athens.
  • Atlanta Combinatorics Colloquium — a joint Georgia Tech, Georgia State, and Emory series for related mathematical foundations.

Online and other seminar series

  • Monte Carlo Online Seminar — Monte Carlo methods and computational statistics.
  • Online Causal Inference Seminar — causal-inference research talks.
  • McGill Statistics Seminar — statistics seminar information and schedules.
  • Centre de recherches mathématiques activities — CRM scientific events and programs.

item.title: GSU faculty in statistics and related fields
item.description:
Statistical research at Georgia State University extends well beyond one department. This directory brings together faculty developing statistical and computational methods and researchers applying quantitative methods to health, brains, education, economics, and business. Use it to discover potential advisors, collaborators, and research questions.

Names are alphabetical by surname within each group, with regular faculty listed before associated and adjunct faculty. Each linked name leads to an official profile, laboratory, or research directory. Faculty associated with Mathematics and Statistics also appear under their related research fields, with their affiliations noted. The groupings are a guide to research connections, rather than formal departmental boundaries. For a broader introduction, see Why study at GSU?.

item.title: Why study at GSU?
item.description:
For students interested in statistics, data science, or AI, Georgia State University combines quantitative training with the opportunities of a major U.S. city. Studying in downtown Atlanta means access to a broad research community, internationally known companies, and plenty to enjoy outside the classroom. Teaching assistantships can also make an MS financially attractive while building valuable teaching experience.

🎓 Build a foundation, then choose an application

The Department of Mathematics and Statistics offers an M.S. in Applied Statistics and a Ph.D. in Mathematics and Statistics, alongside mathematics programs and new machine learning and data science concentrations. This creates routes for students interested in statistical methodology, applications, or the interface between statistics and computation. Explore the department’s programs and compare the M.S. and Ph.D. curricula with your goals.

item.title: Drug discovery: statistics and AI agents
item.description:
Drug discovery connects biological understanding with evidence about candidate compounds, including activity, toxicity, and how compounds behave in the body. These early investigations precede later stages of drug development. [1] A statistical question runs through this process: which candidate or experiment should we investigate next, given limited data and resources?
